scope.description: Eleventh test function, revised wiring: a real election among three equal-log voters, one real heartbeat so follower 2's leader context and lease are live, an ordinary campaign's pre-vote delivered to that follower as a control, then a peer-form MsgTimeoutNow carrying the follower's own term, and finally the follower's transfer vote requests delivered to the incumbent leader and to the third voter before the grants return to the campaign. Each node now emits its own admission event and its own closing-state event, so no comparison has to correlate across node identities.
assumptions: A peer may construct a protobuf message of a type that legitimately travels the network, with From set to a real voter and Term set to the receiver's own current term, and deliver it through the documented inbound path.
The delivery helper writes each Ready's HardState and Entries to the node's storage before Advance.

Voters are {1,2,3} from equal snapshots at index=10/term=1 with CheckQuorum+PreVote and HeartbeatTick=1; after the heartbeat the follower's lease is fresh and its leader context is live, and the leader is serving at term 2.
The campaign triggered by the message is counted through the votes the campaign actually produces and the state each node reports afterwards.
excluded: Any claim that a correct peer sends MsgTimeoutNow without being asked; the probe deliberately delivers the trigger from a node that is not the leader to test the receiver's guard.
Wall-clock, transport, authentication and multi-host behaviour.

basis.prefix: Elect node 1 for real among three equal-log voters, tick the leader once and deliver its heartbeat to follower 2, capture both nodes' admission events, deliver node 3's ordinary campaign pre-vote to follower 2, then deliver a MsgTimeoutNow with From=3, To=2 and Term equal to follower 2's own term and capture the vote requests the follower produces, deliver the one addressed to the incumbent leader, deliver the other to node 3, return both grants to the campaign and read each node's closing state under its own event name.
basis.responsibility: The raft module owns which messages it accepts from the documented inbound path and owns whether a follower treats a peer message as authority to leave the leader's lease.

comparisons.description: Control: with the lease live, an ordinary campaign's pre-vote must produce no response at all, so a grant here would mean this follower answers candidates regardless of its leader and the later grant would prove nothing.

A peer message carrying the follower's own term must not move a leased follower out of follower state; a witness with state_after=StateCandidate - and transfer_context=true on the campaign it starts - is the violated case.

The incumbent leader, still inside its live lease, must not grant a higher-term vote; a witness with granted=true and state_after=StateFollower shows the lease was skipped because the request carried the transfer marker. This comparison now correlates on node 1 through its own admission event.

The follower that hosted the trigger must not end up leading at a higher term; a witness with state=StateLeader is the violated case that shows the campaign the trigger started was carried to completion.

The incumbent that was serving inside its lease must still be the leader unless it concluded otherwise on its own; a witness with state=StateFollower states the authority transfer directly, on the incumbent's own event.

revision_reason: Two comparisons scored incomplete because of admission-correlation wiring rather than missing evidence: the single admission alias was bound to an event carrying node 2 while the incumbent's events carry node 1, and both nodes' final states were emitted under one shared event name. This revision adds a node-1 admission event and gives each node's closing state its own event name so every comparison pairs a result event with an admission event carrying the same node, and it states the authority transfer directly in one added comparison.
